title: Time series momentum in FX majors (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen 2012)
text: Time series momentum: the sign of the past 12-month excess return predicts the next month's return across 58 liquid futures and forward contracts including FX majors; a moving-average cross is the executable proxy. Public literature claim, a hypothesis for the ten gates, not a recipe.

title: Time series momentum in metals and equity indices (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen 2012)
text: Time series momentum holds across asset classes -- metals and equity index futures included -- with the strongest returns during market extremes. Moving-average cross as the executable proxy. Public literature claim.

title: Time series momentum in agricultural commodities (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen 2012)
text: Time series momentum across commodity futures including grains and softs; trend-following managed futures returns are explained by it. Moving-average cross as the executable proxy. Public literature claim.

title: Trend following with volatility targeting (Man AHL research; Moskowitz et al.)
text: Volatility-scaled trend following: position size inversely proportional to trailing volatility so each market contributes equal risk; the Sharpe of trend following improves after volatility targeting and drawdowns shorten. Momentum with a volatility gate is the executable proxy. Public literature claim.

title: Trend following with volatility targeting across equity indices (Man AHL)
text: Volatility-targeted trend following across global equity index futures; momentum with a volatility gate as the executable proxy. Public literature claim.

title: London open breakout of the Asian range (Kakushadze & Serur 2018, FX intraday strategies)
text: Asian session range breakout at the London open: the London session breaks the overnight Asia range with follow-through; session range breakout in the london session is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: New York open range breakout (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Opening range breakout at the New York session open in gold, index CFDs and USDJPY: the first-hour range is broken with follow-through. Session range breakout in the new_york session. Public literature claim.

title: Overnight drift in equity indices (Kakushadze & Serur 2018; Lou, Polk, Skouras 2019)
text: The equity premium accrues overnight: index returns from the close to the next open dominate the day session. Overnight drift is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Day-of-week effects in FX and gold (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Day-of-week seasonality: returns and volatility differ systematically by weekday in FX and gold, with Monday and Friday the anomalous days. Day of week effect is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Weekend gap fade on the Monday open (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: The Monday open gap in FX tends to fill during the Monday session; fading the weekend gap is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Short-term RSI mean reversion in equity indices (Connors; Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Two-day RSI mean reversion: buying an index after the 2-period RSI falls below 10 and selling above 90 captures short-horizon reversal in equity indices. RSI mean reversion is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Bollinger band reversion in range-bound FX crosses (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Bollinger band mean reversion: a close beyond two standard deviations from the moving average reverts toward the band midpoint in low-trend crosses. Bollinger mean reversion is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Range reversion in managed and low-volatility crosses (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Range trading: crosses with policy-anchored or low-volatility regimes revert from the edges of the recent range. Range reversion is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Volatility squeeze breakout (Bollinger squeeze; Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Volatility squeeze: a period of contracting Bollinger bandwidth precedes expansion, and the breakout direction has follow-through. Volatility squeeze is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Pullback entries in an established trend (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Pullback entry: buying a retracement to the moving average inside an up-trend (selling in a down-trend) captures trend continuation with a defined stop. Pullback entry is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Failed breakout reversal / turtle soup (Connors & Raschke; Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Failed breakout: a break of the 20-day high or low that reverses back inside the range the same session tends to continue reversing. Failed breakout is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Previous-day high/low level breakout (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Level breakout: a break of the prior day's high or low with volume carries follow-through in gold, indices and yen crosses. Level breakout is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: London fix / London close momentum in FX (Evans & Lyons fix effects; Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Order flow around the London 4pm fix creates momentum into the fix and partial reversal after it in the majors. London close momentum is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Asian session momentum in yen and antipodean pairs (Kakushadze & Serur 2018)
text: Asian session momentum: Tokyo-session moves in USDJPY and the antipodean pairs persist into the London open. Asia momentum in the asia session is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: US data shock continuation in the New York session (Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold, Vega 2003)
text: Scheduled US macro announcements move the dollar within minutes and the move persists through the session; a USD session shock filter captures the continuation. Public literature claim.

title: Volume spike reversal and continuation (Kakushadze & Serur 2018; Alpha101 volume-price operators)
text: Abnormal tick volume relative to its trailing average marks exhaustion or initiation; the Alpha101 family's rank(correlation(close, volume)) operators are the formulaic ancestors. Volume spike is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Volatility regime transitions (Man Institute; Ang & Bekaert regime switching)
text: Returns differ across volatility regimes and the transition itself is tradeable: entering a high-volatility regime is followed by mean reversion in vol-scaled positions. Vol transition is the executable form. Public literature claim.

title: Turn-of-the-month effect in equity indices (Ariel 1987; McConnell & Xu 2008)
text: Turn of the month: equity index returns concentrate in the last trading day and first three trading days of each month. Turn of month is the executable form. Public literature claim.
